title: An easier way to clear old tasks.
description: Keep your task list focused with reversible cleanup.
items: Archive tasks individually, select a batch, or archive finished tasks matching your filters.
Undo an archive or restore tasks from Archived. Results and workspaces stay available.

title: Keep the ideas coming
description: Capture quick changes in a running conversation while your agent works.
items: Live sessions save messages and drafts, process ordered batches in an isolated workspace, and keep results together for review.
Pop out a compact session window and pin it above other apps. Review cumulative changes as a saved patch.
note: In development. Installed-provider and native-window validation remain in progress.

title: Let the task choose its approach.
description: Start a task without deciding whether to split it first.
items: Lead agents assess useful delegation through available subagent tools and remain responsible for the combined result and checks.
Small or tightly coupled work stays together; saved split plans remain recoverable in feature planning.
note: Delegation depends on the selected provider's available tools. Real-provider validation remains in progress.

title: A simpler task view
description: Follow work and review results in a clearer task layout.
items: See task progress with agent artwork, grouped review tools and concise errors.
Switch attempts and continue work with fewer competing controls.

title: See where your tokens go
description: Usage connects spending to tasks and saved outcomes across your projects.
items: Explore token trends and drill into projects, agents, tasks, and individual calls.
See measured agent-selection overhead, missing reports, and separate Ask Jackalope usage.

title: Clearer agreements between agents.
description: Agents can record ownership handoffs and agree on shared interfaces across separate worktrees.
items: Conflicting ownership claims are rejected, and handoffs require the next owner to accept.
Unresolved interface decisions and changed-file scope checks block dependent work or integration until reconciled.
Projects can opt into agent reconciliation and verified local merges while retaining the original worktrees.
note: Installed-app acceptance and broader cross-provider evaluation remain in progress.

title: Window control on GNOME Wayland
description: Ubuntu GNOME 46 gains scoped window control through an optional Jackalope extension.
items: Choose a window and resume from a visible native bar, with typing, clicks, scrolling, accessibility and window capture.
Keyboard or pointer activity pauses control; Escape, connection loss and extension disable end access.
note: Real-device and installation testing remain open. Other Wayland desktops are not supported yet.

title: Match agent effort to the task
description: Task effort now requests matching reasoning levels from Codex and Claude, with clearer usage records and more reliable long checks.
items: Quick, Balanced and Thorough apply to the launched agent without changing global settings.
Saved verification has time to finish, and usage exports retain effort and verification output measurements.

title: A guided start with local AI
description: An optional path to trying Jackalope without an AI provider subscription, with clear requirements and download choices.
items: Check your computer, set up OpenCode and Ollama, and verify a local file edit and continued session before connecting.
Keep model downloads optional. Jackalope bundles no model weights.
Retrieve relevant help locally and reduce repeated routing context while preserving eligible models and task requirements.
note: Real-model quality, paid-token savings and installed setup remain under validation.

title: Native window control beyond Windows
description: macOS and Linux X11 window-control backends are implemented for native validation.
items: Keep explicit window grants, visible Pause/Resume/Cancel controls, fresh snapshots, and physical-input interruption.
Check device readiness, request macOS permissions, and use platform-appropriate shortcut labels.
Exercise Linux control against isolated native windows in CI.
note: macOS compilation and device acceptance remain open. Wayland window control still requires a compositor-specific implementation; public availability is unchanged.

title: Know which desktop is connected.
description: Connected desktops now shows app and profile details to help identify separate installations and test profiles.
items: See app version, platform, profile type, connection expiry, and recent account and settings checks.

title: More focused task guidance and verification
description: Task instructions stay closer to your request, and long successful checks return compact results with stored output available when needed.
items: Automatic guidance distinguishes design tokens from security work and avoids adding debugging routines to spelling fixes.
Agents use the assigned workspace and receive tool instructions appropriate to their connection.
Independent native trials compare correctness and total reported usage against a preserved baseline.
Codex can run the saved project check during a task, so it can inspect failures before finishing.
note: In development. Broader provider comparisons and installed-app acceptance remain in progress.

title: Smoother task history and review
description: Task updates and large histories do less work in the desktop interface.
items: Task output uses durable incremental saves, and the interface receives changed task records.
History loads concurrently, while large patches and code highlighting run in background workers.

title: Better coordination from request to review.
description: Feature plans preserve the complete request and can continue from verified predecessor snapshots.
items: Independent work shares capacity fairly, while verification reserves only its workspace.
Structured handoffs and execution timings make progress and results easier to inspect.

title: Kimi Code joins the workspace
description: Use Kimi for tasks and routing, with broader tool and usage coverage across existing agents.
items: Choose Kimi accounts and models, respond to approvals and structured questions, continue sessions, and read task tokens and membership quota.
Connect project tools directly to Kimi and OpenCode, discover Grok models, and read Antigravity subscription quota.
note: Authenticated installed-app acceptance remains in progress; provider and CLI limits apply.

title: Account access in every build.
description: Development and release builds now use the same account access checks.
items: Connect an approved account before starting new work, with verified offline access and saved-work recovery preserved.

title: More at home on every desktop.
description: Task notifications, accounts, and background cleanup now cover more of the macOS and Linux experience.
items: Open the matching task from native macOS and Linux notifications.
Account connections and settings sync are enabled across platforms.
Unix task groups gain crash cleanup, with better Linux tray and macOS Dock recovery.
note: Desktop-control backends and installed-platform acceptance are still in progress.

title: Preparing for more desktops.
description: Cross-platform foundations are ready for native testing on macOS and Linux.
items: Improved agent and browser detection, terminal cleanup, secure account storage, and notifications.
Added native CI checks and trial packages for Linux and Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.
note: Desktop control still requires macOS and Linux backends. Signed releases and installed-device acceptance remain in progress.

title: Project lessons grounded in your work
description: Jackalope learns from local task feedback and repository evidence, and shows recorded findings in Performance & insights.
items: Matching lessons retain their sources and can be edited, paused, removed or skipped.
Performance distinguishes finished runs from human outcome decisions and removes invented savings and generic recommendations.

title: A predictable local work cycle
description: Completed tasks get automatic checkpoints, followed by a reviewed merge and safe worktree cleanup.
items: Choose agent, shared or user-only commit credit per project during setup.
Review automatic commit messages and merge a task group as one commit.
Detect already integrated content and remove completed worktrees and branches; one failed folder no longer stops bulk cleanup.
note: Development milestone; installed-agent acceptance remains open.

title: Hourly recurring tasks
description: Schedule regular checks without writing a cron expression.
items: Choose intervals of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 or 12 hours and a minute past the hour.
Timing follows clock hours in the selected timezone and retains existing missed-run policies.

title: Ask Jackalope from your workspace.
description: Your companion connects your configured agent to official help and reviewed app actions.
items: Ask questions with documentation sources, preview appearance changes and adjust supported preferences.
Prepare task drafts, open or stop shared tasks, navigate the app and change the default agent through reviewed actions.
Connect external agents through an expiring local MCP connection, or copy website guides as Markdown.

title: Explore where Jackalope goes next.
description: An interactive roadmap connects the workspace we have built with the release work and ideas ahead.
items: Explore built, in-progress, planned, and exploratory work with expandable feature details.
A branded journey makes current priorities and future possibilities easier to follow.

title: Smarter project settings.
description: Repository context helps fill project setup defaults.
items: Detect preparation and verification commands from documentation and manifests, and the target branch from local Git metadata.
Preserve saved choices and deliberately cleared fields when refreshing context.

title: Practical guides for working with coding agents.
description: Five longer reads cover worktrees, working with two agents, code review, MCP connections and choosing a workspace.
items: Follow worked examples, reusable prompts and checklists with authoritative references.
Navigate article sections and explore related guides and app comparisons.

title: A fresh look around Jackalope
description: Explore the updated app in a new 64-second product tour.
items: See themes, project setup, task dispatch, browser evidence, agent accounts, and the interactive codebase map.
Watch bold animated feature cards with an original upbeat soundtrack, a new poster, and descriptive captions.
note: The walkthrough uses sample workspace data and scripted browser interactions.

title: See all your agent accounts together
description: Existing CLI logins and added accounts now share one account list with detected identities and editable names.
items: Rename, label and group the existing CLI account just like an added account.
Agents cards show account identities, total counts and overlapping icons for multiple accounts.
Keep task customization visible while retaining automatic setup defaults.

title: Describe the task and let Jackalope handle setup
description: Task creation now puts your intent first, with a compact setup summary and optional customization.
items: Use automatic agent, model and account routing with inherited project tools and matching lessons.
Project tools no longer need a per-task checklist; saved restrictions remain intact until explicitly reset.
Find effort, workspace and agent overrides under Customize task.

title: Clearer worktree cleanup
description: Clean up merged worktrees when only disposable build output or dependencies remain.
items: See which worktrees are ready and which generated folders cleanup removes.
Keep local edits, configuration and unrecognized ignored files protected, including during archive and remove.

title: Connect once, set up each project.
description: Check early access and app privacy on launch, then set up projects with their own agent choices.
items: An animated access check leads into reusable Project, Agent and First task steps, with a project default and switches for detected agents.
New connections default to settings sync, with an opt-out before connecting and saved opt-outs preserved.
Sync appearance and notification choices with strict privacy controls and conflict review.
Delete the saved settings copy and disable sync across connected desktops.

title: Your project at a glance
description: Repository knowledge is easier to scan and turn into work.
items: Project Context groups source files, technologies, instructions and commands in a visual overview.
Lessons and workflows use compact cards with full content available on demand.
Repo TODOs offer a Start task action with prefilled context. Completion moves into explicit edit controls, with Cancel and Discard beside the document heading.

title: Stay in control of desktop assistance.
description: A clear status bar and theme-colored glow show when Jackalope is using your computer.
items: Pause or cancel from the top bar, press Escape to cancel, and explicitly resume after mouse, keyboard or window interruptions.
Larger display-scaled text and working controls keep desktop assistance readable.
note: Desktop assistance requires Windows and permission for each window.

title: Guides and help, close at hand
description: Find answers about Jackalope in a searchable knowledgebase, with direct access from the desktop app.
items: Search guides, visual architecture diagrams, and troubleshooting recipes across nine feature categories.
Access the Knowledgebase directly from the desktop shell using the new header life preserver shortcut, the Command Palette, or Settings.

title: Task routing with quota awareness
description: Jackalope's default agent can select an enabled agent, configured model and account for automatic tasks.
items: Uses reported quota headroom and local active-work reservations when admitting work.
Hands quota-interrupted tasks to an eligible fallback in the same workspace with progress and usage retained.
Shows routing decisions and attributes routing and worker usage separately.
note: Explicit assignments stay pinned. Missing quota is treated as unknown.

title: Palettes that follow your color.
description: Choose Single, Duo or Trio to build a coordinated theme from one primary color.
items: Companion colors and workspace gradients update as you explore the color picker.
Palette previews preserve cancel, reset and saved themes, with readable action labels on hover.

title: Your next hop into Jackalope.
description: Track your waitlist place, bring people along, and share Instant Access Passes once you are in.
items: Verified waitlist referrals earn priority, with progress visible on your access page.
Accepted members get five passes to bring people straight into early access.
Clear emails guide verification, referral milestones, pass claims, and expired reservations.

title: More of the work, in one place.
description: The current development build brings task work and project context into a more focused workspace.
items: Tasks groups active work, saved evidence, and recurring work. Project holds codebase exploration, worktrees, and context.
Project tool selections can travel with Codex and Claude Code task launches, while existing CLI-global tools remain available.
Recurring work includes timezone and missed-run controls. The app must remain running; it cannot wake a closed app or a sleeping computer.
Account-aware usage views and locally bundled fonts are part of the current development build.
note: Scheduled work requires Jackalope to stay running.

title: A first look at Jackalope.
description: A place to explore the product and follow what comes next.
items: Real interface captures in light and dark appearances, using an explicitly fictional Atlas project.
An interactive recorded tour covering task drafting, patch review, agent selection, and the live theme palette.
A three-step introduction, product notes, and an early-access waitlist.
note: The walkthrough illustrates the interface with sample data.
